 Cavs Notes: Hezonja, Mobley, Altman, Thomas
 By Luke Adams |
 at October 31, 2026 9:11 am 
 Mario Hezonja ’s one-year, minimum-salary contract remains non-guaranteed until November 15 , but based on the role the Croatian forward is playing so far this season, he has made that decision an easy one for the Cavaliers , according to Chris Fedor of Cleveland.com (subscription required).
 In his first NBA stint since 2020 following six years in Europe, Hezonja is averaging 7.4 points and 4.0 rebounds in 17.4 minutes per game while shooting a career-best 35.3% on three-pointers through five appearances off the bench. He has played between 15 and 20 minutes in each of those five games as he establishes himself as a regular part of head coach Kenny Atkinson ’s rotation.
 “It’s a hard transformation,” Atkinson said of Hezonja’s transition from EuroLeague star to NBA role player. “I think he’s doing great, honestly. He’s going to find his niche because the talent is obviously there, and he’s going to help us win I think a lot of games. Just right now it’s early. He’s still getting to know everybody. We’re getting to know him as coaches, where he fits, and as we get to know each other better, it’ll improve the whole thing.” 
 Given how little breathing room the Cavaliers have below their first-apron hard cap, waiving Hezonja in order to replace him with a new 14th man wouldn’t have been ideal, but it would have been possible. At this point though, it’s a safe bet he’ll remain under contract through November 15, which would guarantee his full $2,845,883 salary and lock in his $2,449,421 cap hit.
 We have more on the Cavaliers:
 Evan Mobley has won a Defensive Player of the Year award, made two All-Defensive first teams, and averaged over 18 points in each of the last two seasons, but if the 25-year-old’s career-high three-point rate so far this season is real, it could meaningfully increase both his and the Cavaliers’ ceiling, Fedor writes for Cleveland.com (subscription required). Even after going 0-for-3 in Thursday’s loss to Atlanta, Mobley has converted 12-of-21 three-pointers through five games. It’s safe to assume he won’t shoot 57.1% from beyond the arc all season, but Mobley said this week that he feels like his improvements are “sustainable,” while teammate Jarret Allen suggested the need for opponents to defend Mobley out to the perimeter “opens the floor up to me.”
 In an in-depth conversation with Terry Pluto of Cleveland.com (subscription required), Cavaliers president of basketball operations Koby Altman – who is in his 10th season running the team’s front office – revisits his tenure as the team’s top basketball decision-maker, detailing the challenges of moving on from the LeBron James era in 2018 and explaining why he’s proud of the fact that Cleveland became a perennial playoff team and legitimate contender just a few years after James’ departure. “Not only did we lose LeBron (without getting anything in return), but we also had massive contracts on the books from our deep runs in the playoffs,” Altman said. “… We drafted Evan (in 2021) and we’ve been a playoff team ever since. When a generational player like LeBron leaves, no one expects you to get back to the playoffs that fast. But we’ve been able to do it and we haven’t looked back.” 
 After scoring double-digit points in his first two NBA games on Monday and Wednesday, Meleek Thomas sat out on Thursday due to right foot inflammation and soreness. The rookie guard, who has a strong +10.2 net rating through his first two outings, is listed as questionable to play in Saturday’s contest in Milwaukee.
